To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chronic mild TBI is associated with loss of white matter tract integrity, particularly crossing fiber integrity, in Iraq and Afghanistan veterans with comorbid depression and PTSD.

chronic mild TBI, in the context of PTSD and depression, is associated with loss of white matter structural integrity that is distributed across multiple fiber bundles, including those in the brainstem and cerebellum.
chronic mild TBI is associated with widespread loss of white matter fiber integrity, and the loss of integrity is correlated with duration of unconsciousness and feeling dazed or confused.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of mild TBI in Iraq and Afghanistan veterans, a population that is at increased risk for chronic TBI.
the effects of blast‐related TBI on brain function and structure.
the study of the effects of blast‐induced mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) on the integrity of white matter in the brains of Iraq and Afghanistan war‐zone veterans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is evidence of white matter damage in the brains of veterans with mild TBI.
the present study provides evidence that chronic mild TBI is associated with loss of white matter structural integrity.
the present results provide evidence of a widespread loss of white matter structural integrity in veterans with a history of chronic mild TBLI and comorbid PTSD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chronic blast‐related mild TBIs in military veterans from Iraq and Afganistan are associated with widespread loss of white matter fiber integrity.
chronic mild TBI is associated with loss of white matter tract integrity in a distributed pattern of brain white matter tracts, and the extent of loss is related to the duration of loss of awareness.

chronic mild TBI, as diagnosed in military veterans with no overt lesions on brain MRI, is characterized by diffuse damage in white matter tracts that is associated with the duration of loss of conscious, but not with PTSD or depression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have found evidence of white matter damage in veterans with mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) that was widespread, and not localized to the area of injury.
the brain of veterans with chronic mild T.B.I. is not the same as the brain of veterans without T.B.I.
we have found a pattern of damage that is consistent with systemic damage from blast‐related TBI.
